new_name.description: If renaming the function, its new name (only letters, digits and underscores, not starting with a digit). Every use of it in the events is updated.

delete_this_function.description: Optional boolean. If true, the function is deleted: the events using it become invalid until they are fixed. Destructive: only set this when the user has explicitly and unambiguously asked to delete it.

changed_settings.description: A list of settings of the function to change. `isPrivate`, `isAsync` and `isDeprecated` take "true" or "false" (the events of an `isAsync` function must run `BuiltinAsync::ResolveAsyncEventsFunction()` once its work is done); `functionType` takes one of `Action`, `Condition`, `Expression`, `StringExpression`, `ExpressionAndCondition`, `ActionWithOperator`; `expressionType` takes `number` (also spelled `expression`, as the project reports it) or `string` and is only for a function returning a value (an `Expression`, a `StringExpression` or an `ExpressionAndCondition`) - a function that stops returning a value (`Action`, `Condition`, `ActionWithOperator`) loses its return type and returns a number again if it becomes an expression later, pass `expressionType` in the same call to choose; `sentence` uses the `_PARAMn_` placeholders; `getterName` is the `ExpressionAndCondition` of an `ActionWithOperator`.

changed_parameters.description: A list of parameters of the function to add, change, reorder or delete. Not for an `ActionWithOperator`: it takes the parameters of its getter (change them on the getter, they reach its actions with operator, calls included).

parameter_name.description: The name of the parameter to change, or of the parameter to add if the function has none with this name.

new_name.description: If renaming the parameter, its new name. The events using it are updated.

delete_this_parameter.description: If true, the parameter is removed. The events and the calls using it must be fixed afterwards.

type.description: The type of the parameter (required when adding one). A `behavior` parameter always applies to the object parameter declared before it.

label.description: The text shown to the user for this parameter in the events editor.

long_description.description: A longer explanation of the parameter, shown to the user.

extra_info.description: The object type for an `objectList` parameter, the behavior type for a `behavior` parameter, `scene` or `object` for an `identifier`, a JSON array of choices for `stringWithSelector` and `numberWithChoices`.

optional.description: If true, the user can leave the parameter empty (`default_value` is then used).

default_value.description: The value used when an optional parameter is left empty, always as a string.

new_index.description: The new position of the parameter among the parameters of the function, 0 being the first one. The implicit `Object` and `Behavior` parameters are not counted.

functions.name: run_gameplay_test
functions.description: Run one gameplay test in a real game preview (the editor exports the project, boots the preview and executes the test against the gameplay test harness). Returns the result object: status (`passed`/`failed`/`error`/`stopped`/`timeout`), framesExecuted, durationMs, assertions, errors, consoleLogs, eventLog, finalState and optional screenshots. When `source` is provided, the test is created/updated (persisted into the project or extension when `persist` is true, the default) and then run. Without `source`, the existing test with `test_name` is run as stored.

scope.description: The tests container the test belongs to: the project itself, or one of its events-based extensions.

extension_name.description: The name of the events-based extension (required when `type` is 'extension').

test_name.description: The name of the test to run (unique in its scope).

source.description: The JavaScript body executed as `async (harness) => { ... }` — the BODY only, never the wrapper function itself. OMIT this to run the stored test code as-is (the normal way to run an existing test). When provided, the test is created/updated with this source — OVERWRITING the stored code when `persist` is true — then run: only do this to author a new test or to fix a test whose previous run could not execute.

description.description: Short description of what the test verifies (stored with the test when it is created/updated).

persist.description: Whether the created/updated test is saved into the project/extension (default true).

timeout_ms.description: Wall-clock timeout for the run, in milliseconds (default 30000, maximum 120000).

functions.name: generate_events
functions.description: Adds new events (conditions and actions), or rework one or more events of the event sheet of a scene, of external events or of a function of an extension, based on "EventScript". This will translate "EventScript" into functional event(s), either new events or replacing existing ones. Get the event ID or group names from the explorer agent first to know where to place the events. If the "EventScript" does not compile, its errors are returned to you and NOTHING is applied: fix the script and call again (a one-line fix, usually). If the corrected script still does not compile, a slower sub-agent takes over and fixes it, then reports what it applied along with the errors of your script. This sub-agent does have not have full context of the game, so you must be precise: include object names, list the extensions that will be used in `extension_names_list`, include precise variable names. Do not invent name of conditions or actions or parameters. For sounds/musics to play, you can first ask the explorer agent to search the resource store for existing audio files, then reference the exact name of the chosen file. To change a part of an existing event (some lines of a `js` event, an action of a long event), use `edits` rather than resending the whole event.

scope.description: Where the events are added or edited: a scene, external events (written with the objects and variables of their associated scene, or else of a scene linking to them), or the extension, custom behavior or custom object owning the function named by `function_name`. Set `type` and the name field(s) of that type.

type.description: `scene`: a scene (`scene_name`). `external_events`: external events (`external_events_name`): events not tied to a scene, included in scenes by `link` events. Usually not recommended. `extension`: an extension of the project (`extension_name`): its free functions and extension variables. `custom_behavior`: a custom behavior of an extension (`extension_name` + `custom_behavior_name`). `custom_object`: a custom object of an extension (`extension_name` + `custom_object_name`): its declaration and functions.

external_events_name.description: The name of the external events (type `external_events`).

extension_name.description: The name of the extension (extension, custom_behavior, custom_object and custom_object_variant types).

custom_behavior_name.description: The name of the custom behavior in the extension (type `custom_behavior`).

custom_object_name.description: The name of the custom object in the extension (custom_object and custom_object_variant types).

function_name.description: The name of the function whose events should be added or edited. Required with a `scope` of type `extension` (a free function), `custom_behavior` or `custom_object`. Unused with a `scene` or `external_events` scope.

event_batches.description: One entry per logical group of events to emit. Each entry has its own placement. Use multiple entries when a single request needs events placed in different locations (e.g., replacing one event AND adding new ones elsewhere). No more than 6 entries.

event_script.description: The events written in the "events script" syntax (see the documentation in your instructions). When valid, the events are created instantly, without any agent working on them - so prefer it whenever you know the exact conditions/actions to use. If it does not compile, the errors are returned to you (nothing applied): fix and call again. Only a second failing attempt is handed to the (slower) agent.

events_description.description: A pseudo-code of the desired events logic, for the rare case where "events script" would not work. This is read by the agent and can also be used to indicate event(s) to remove or rework. Not needed if `event_script` is given. Avoid using it.

placement_relation.description: Structural tree operation. Sub-events relations nest under the target — new events inherit its conditions and object picking. Sibling relations place next to the target with the same parent — new events inherit only the parent's conditions, NOT the target's. To rework an existing event, prefer `replace_event_but_keep_existing_sub_events`: it replaces the event (conditions, actions, local variables) and re-attaches its existing sub-events, unmodified, to the first new event — so do NOT include the sub-events in your script (they would be duplicated). Use `replace_entire_event_and_sub_events` only to rework an event AND all its sub-events: everything not in your script is deleted, so your script must contain the full subtree you want to keep (read it first with `read_events_source`). Use `append_to_end` to add the events at the end of the events of the scope (the scene, the external events or the function).

expected_event_source.description: REQUIRED with the replace relations and an `event_script` (not with `edits`): the CURRENT source of what you are replacing, as returned by `read_events_source`. With `replace_event_but_keep_existing_sub_events`: the event itself, WITHOUT its sub-events. With `replace_entire_event_and_sub_events`: the event WITH all its sub-events. Whitespace, line breaks, casing, `#` comments and `pass` lines are ignored. Proves what you replace was read and has not changed: the call is REJECTED (nothing applied) on mismatch, with the current source in the answer.

placement_target_event_id.description: Reference event ID or group name. Required for all relations except append_to_end. Meaning depends on relation: parent for append_subevents_to; sibling anchor for insert_*_sibling; event being replaced for the replace relations or delete. If unsure, call `read_events_source` to get the event ID.

placement_expected_parent_event_id.description: Safety check: The ID of the event (or group name) that must end up as the direct parent of the inserted events after placement. Use empty string for top-level scene events. If unsure, don't specify this field.

placement_rationale.description: One sentence explaining why this placement is correct with respect to inherited parent conditions and object picking. Example: "Sibling of event-2.5 (not 2.5.1) because these events check State='XXX' and must not inherit event-2.5's State='YYY' condition."

edits.description: Instead of `event_script`, with a replace relation: exact text replacements in the CURRENT source of the event, as `read_events_source` returns it - the code of a `js` event (also given as numbered lines in `jsCodeExcerpt`: never copy the numbers), the "events script" of any other event (without its sub-events with `replace_event_but_keep_existing_sub_events`, with them with `replace_entire_event_and_sub_events`). Applied in order; if one fails, nothing is changed. The code of a `js` event is changed directly, whatever its size: give the `edits` of `js` events in a call of their own. The answer says how many occurrences each edit replaced, at which lines, and gives the numbered lines around the changes (`editedEventSnippets`).

old_string.description: The exact text to replace. It must be found once: include lines around it to make it unique (or set `replace_all`).

extension_names_list.description: A comma-separated list of the exact type of extensions (including built-in ones), behaviors, and/or objects that will be used in the event (e.g: `Sprite, PhysicsCharacter3D, PhysicsCharacter3D::PhysicsCharacter3D, ParticleSystem::ParticleEmitter, BuiltinMouse` - can be arbitrarily long to list everything needed).

objects_list.description: A comma-separated list of the exact name of objects (scene, global objects...) or groups that will be used in the events (probably those mentioned in the events description, but there can be more if you think they are useful). Example: `Player, Obstacle, Enemy1, RedCoin, GreenCoin, Super_Enemy`. These objects (or groups) must all already be part of the game (if not, please use the "edit" agent first to build these objects, add behaviors, etc...).

estimated_complexity.description: Estimated complexity of the requested events generation, from 0 to 100. Example: editing a parameter value in an event with 3 actions: 6, 1 new condition and 1 new action or less: 12, 2 events max with 6 actions/conditions: 22, more events or loops: 40, large algorithm or many concerns in the request: 82, very large algorithm or many tasks, would need splitting work: 93. Will be used for estimating the work effort.

functions.name: run_script
functions.description: Run a JavaScript script calling the editor functions described in the system prompt (and only them — no other API is available). The script is executed in the GDevelop editor, against the currently opened project. Use `await` for every function call — calls run sequentially, in order. Execution STOPS at the first function call returning `success: false` or at the first thrown error: everything executed before is applied (there is no rollback), and you receive the outputs of all the calls made so far, the failure details (function name, arguments, error and line number), plus everything logged with `console.log`. Inspect function results in the script (e.g. `const result = await inspect_variables({...}); console.log(result.variables);`) and log what you need to see. Prefer one script doing several steps over many single-call scripts, but stay reasonable: if a later step depends on information you cannot check in the script, stop the script there and read the outputs first.

title.description: A 4-10 word summary of what this script does, shown to the user while it runs (write it in their language). Start with a verb.

js_code.description: The JavaScript code to run. Top-level `await` is allowed (the script body is treated as an async function). Call only the editor functions from the API definition and standard JavaScript (no DOM, no fetch, no imports). A `return` value, if any, is reported back to you along with the console logs and each function call output.
